messages:
Olivia: Heads up — I'm drafting the canary schedule for model v2 -> v2.1 upgrade. Proposing a low initial exposure + conservative guards. want early engineering + SRE eyes :eyes:
Raj: share the percent steps you have in mind?
Olivia: thinking: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 40% -> 100%. steps are 20m, 20m, 40m, 60m (can pause). rationale: avoid noisy spikes and give telemetry time to settle.
Matt: 0.5% initial seems fine for risky changes, but 20m might be short for embeddings-heavy endpoints (cold caches). could we add a metric-based minimum duration?
Jena: agree on metric-based guards. SRE asks to trigger pause/rollback if 95th latency increases > 20% OR error rate (5xx+model-timeouts) > 1.5% over baseline. Also require token-level cost delta alert (if cost up by >15%).
Olivia: proposed guard snippet (for the rollout engine):
```
canary: {
  steps: [0.5, 2, 10, 40, 100],
  step_durations: [20m, 20m, 40m, 60m, 0m],
  pause_on_failure: true,
  guards: {
    latency_p95_pct_increase: 20,
    error_rate_pct: 1.5,
    cost_pct_increase: 15,
    minimum_samples_per_step: 500
  }
}
```
Raj: minimum_samples_per_step is important. For low traffic customers we should default to a time-based fallback (i.e., if samples < N after T minutes, auto-skip or extend?).
Matt: Maybe default: if samples < 500 after 30m, extend step by 30m automatically once, then mark manual review if still low. Saves us from silent under-sampling.
Uxana: UX question — in the Console, how do we present this? I suggest showing both the percentage timeline and a live "guard status" row that can be clicked to see failing metrics and quick rollback button. Also allow an explicit "manual advance" and a "pause & inspect" action.
Jena: +1 on manual controls. For policy we need both a safety auto-rollback and a soft-pause that alerts the owners and asks for manual confirm to continue.
Olivia: agree. Want default to auto-pause (not auto-rollback) except for severe errors (e.g., model crashing or >5% absolute error-rate) where we auto-rollback. Add that to guards.
Raj: small API detail — rollout config in infra currently expects percentages as ints (1,5,10...), not floats. We'll need to update the schema for fractional initial canaries (0.5). Should we accept per-mille instead?
Matt: per-mille is fine. Schema change: traffic_unit: [percent|permille] and value typed as int. less surface area for floats.
Olivia: good call. I'll update the frontend form to show "0.5% (5‰)" when permille is selected.
ci-bot: Deployment pipeline check: new canary-config schema change will trigger breaking checks in staging. See CI job #4621 — will run integration tests on rollout engine. :robot_face:
Jena: action items: 1) Raj to propose schema PR for permille support. 2) Matt to implement sample/fallback extension logic in rollout engine. 3) Uxana + Olivia to mock console UI with guard row. 4) SRE (Jena) to finalize metric thresholds and add playbook entries.
Raj: I'll open the schema PR today and include backward compatibility migration for existing int-percent configs.
Matt: I'll prototype the sample-based extension behavior and push a feature flag.
Uxana: mockups by EOD Thursday. Will include quick-rollback affordance and a small inline explanation for each guard.
Olivia: one more thing — telemetry: we should emit per-step sampling counts and an aggregated "canary_health_score" (0-100) so downstream alerting + cost dashboards can show a unified signal.
Jena: yes. health_score should combine latency/error/cost with configurable weights. we'll default weights to {latency:0.5, error:0.35, cost:0.15}.
Raj: quick API example to apply canary config (internal):
```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/rollouts" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"proj-xyz/v2.1","traffic_unit":"permille","steps":[5,20,100,400,1000],"step_durations_minutes":[20,20,40,60,0],"guards":{...}}'
```
Olivia: looks good. Anything else before I turn this into a formal RFC?
Matt: add a note about exponential vs linear ramps — some customers prefer geometric steps for fast rollouts. leave it configurable but pick our conservative default as above.
Uxana: and include a short in-console help tooltip explaining why first step is tiny (data quality + sampling).
Olivia: cool. I'll write the RFC and link the mockups + PRs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
